venue: arXiv (Northeastern University NLP course project, not peer-reviewed venue)
benchmarks: Repository-Level Prompt Generation benchmark (47 Java repos, 189,557 holes)

key_numbers.value: 57% (RepoCoder, GPT-3.5-Turbo) vs 40.56% no-retrieval baseline
68.51% (RLPG-H) vs 58.73% Codex baseline; oracle upper bound 79.63%

budget_tradeoff_detail: none reported (review discusses accuracy/success-rate gains of the two surveyed systems, not token-cost tradeoffs)
confound_note: Review juxtaposes two independently published systems (RLPG's learned classifier over rule-based context proposers vs RepoCoder's iterative BM25 similarity retrieval) that differ in representation, mechanism, dataset, and base model simultaneously; it is a narrative synthesis of separately reported numbers, not a controlled single comparison.
stop_detail: Sec. 2 'Repository Level Retrieval Techniques': RLPG selects among rule-based context proposers (parent/child/sibling/import/similar-name files) via a learned classifier (RLPG-H/R), while RepoCoder iteratively retrieves BM25-similar snippets using the model's own prior generation as the next query.
threats_to_datum: This is a non-peer-reviewed student course-project literature review synthesizing numbers from the underlying RLPG/RepoCoder papers rather than running new experiments; extracted via automated WebFetch summarization, not manually checked against the original papers.

demote_reason: Full text confirms retrieval and context operate at single-function/contract granularity for formal-verification property generation (embedding-based retrieval of similar human-written properties for one-shot ICL), not repository-scale structural context budgeting; authors state the approach works on 'typically one function' at a time with no cross-file dependency management or token-budget tradeoff for codebase context.

key_numbers.value: CodeLlama-7B: +16% infile lines, +53% inproject lines vs no-context
17% successful fixes (GPT-3.5)

budget_tradeoff_detail: none explicitly reported as a token/cost-vs-quality curve; each task defines its own baseline context-assembly strategy (BM25 top-20 API names, 7-line error context, files closest in file tree, embedding/TF-IDF retrieval) without a unified budget accounting.
confound_note: Six independent benchmark tasks each vary both the underlying model and the context-assembly strategy (raw window vs BM25/embedding retrieval vs full-repo file lists) simultaneously; this is a multi-task benchmark suite of separate baselines, not one controlled ablation.
stop_detail: Sec. 3-4: each of six tasks defines its own project-wide context mechanism, e.g. BM25-retrieved top-20 relevant class/method names for library-based generation, files closest in the file tree to the target for project completion, and TF-IDF/CodeBERT/GTE/Mistral embedding retrieval plus BM25 for bug localization.
threats_to_datum: Numbers extracted via automated HTML-to-text summarization rather than manual table verification; cross-task comparisons conflate model choice and representation/mechanism differences.

venue: Submitted to ACM TOSEM (not yet accepted)
demote_reason: Full text shows the knowledge graph indexes repository metadata only (entities: Users, Commits, Issues, Files; relations: Author, Assigned, Introduced, Fixed, Changed) for a GraphRAG-style natural-language Q&A system over development activity (e.g., 'who contributed', 'which commit fixed bug X'), not source-code structure; there is no code-content context budgeting or cross-file structural representation of a codebase for a code-generation/editing LLM.

budget_tradeoff_detail: none reported (no explicit token/context-window budget numbers given)
confound_note: Compares the proposed knowledge-graph hybrid retrieval against a no-context baseline and an EvoCodeBench text-retrieval baseline; representation, mechanism, and evaluation sample count (275 vs CodeXGraph's 212) all vary simultaneously, not a budget-matched single-variable ablation.
stop_detail: Repository parsed via AST into a graph of File/Class/Method/Function/Attribute nodes plus LLM-generated descriptions; at query time, full-text index + vector embeddings (all-MiniLM) identify seed nodes, graph n-hop expansion pulls related structure, and semantic ranking filters the sub-graph, which is inserted into the prompt (Sec. Pipeline/Methodology).
threats_to_datum: Peer-review status inferred from an IEEE workshop DOI rather than an explicit acceptance statement in the paper text; numbers extracted via automated HTML summarization, not direct table inspection.

key_numbers.value: masking 54.8% solve / -52.7% cost vs LLM-summary 53.8% solve / -50.4% cost
7-11% additional cost reduction vs masking/summary alone, +2.6pp solve rate (SWE-bench Verified-50, Qwen3-Coder 480B)

budget_tradeoff_detail: Masking cuts cost ~50-56% relative to the raw (uncompressed) agent while matching or slightly exceeding LLM-summarization's solve rate across five model configurations on SWE-bench Verified (Sec. 4).
confound_note: Central comparison varies the context-management mechanism (fixed-window observation masking vs LLM-generated running summary) at run time; token budget/cost is the measured outcome rather than a held-constant control variable across arms.
stop_detail: Sec. 3.1: masking replaces environment observations older than a fixed window of M turns with a placeholder, while LLM-Summary replaces older turns beyond N+M turns with a periodically regenerated LLM-produced running summary plus a few recent turns in full (Eq. 3-6).
threats_to_datum: Numbers read via automated HTML-to-text summarization rather than manual table verification; the novel hybrid approach's numbers are reported only on a 50-instance SWE-bench Verified subset, not the full 500-instance set.

venue: Workshop on LLM Assisted Security and Trust Exploration (LAST-X) 2026
demote_reason: Full text confirms the entire study operates at function-level in-context-learning example selection for vulnerability detection (PrimeVul, DiverseVul, SVEN datasets); the authors explicitly list function-level scope as a stated limitation versus repository-level detection, and the paper never addresses multi-file dependencies, call graphs, or repository-scale token/context budgeting.

benchmarks: two private enterprise repositories (DataB C/C++, etc.)

key_numbers.metric: Levenshtein distance (function-call completion, DataB C/C++, Granite-8B)
key_numbers.value: optimal 42 vs baseline 84; full distance 45 vs 9,834
customized 8B models outperform uncustomized 72B Qwen2.5 across most categories
prefix capped at 3KB; semantic-scope units 50-1,000 bytes

budget_tradeoff_detail: With prefix capped at 3KB and scope granularity 50-1,000 bytes, a customized 8B model beats an uncustomized 72B baseline on completion accuracy (Results section).
confound_note: RAG vs fine-tuning arms differ in mechanism (retrieval vs weight update) while sharing the same AST/bracket-derived 'semantic scope' chunking; the customization-approach vs baseline-model-size comparison conflates model scale and customization method rather than isolating representation alone.
stop_detail: Sec. 3: repository code is segmented into language-independent 'semantic scopes' derived from AST/bracket-matching (function bodies, loop bodies, conditionals; 50-1,000 bytes), which become either the retrieval unit for an embedding-based RAG index (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, top-3/5 nearest neighbors) or the label half of (prefix, scope) fine-tuning pairs.
threats_to_datum: Numbers extracted via automated HTML-summarization from tables covering private industrial repositories that may not render precisely; benchmark comparisons mix customization-method and model-size confounds.

key_numbers.metric: issue resolution rate vs no compression
key_numbers.value: GPT-5.2: 0.578, +4.6pp / +9.2% relative; DeepSeek-V3.2: 0.522, +4.4pp; Qwen3-Coder: 0.420, +2.0pp
6.03x-6.55x across three models

budget_tradeoff_detail: At ~6x compression (51.8-71.3% token reduction), SWEzze improves SWE-bench Verified issue resolution 5.0-9.2% relative over the no-compression baseline; competing baselines target similar ~5-6x ratios but their achieved compression varies widely (LLMLingua-2 ~2.98x, SWE-Pruner 4.10-49.75x), so budgets are not matched exactly across methods (Table 2-3).
confound_note: Central comparison varies the compression mechanism (learned segment-relevance filtering vs generic token-level LLMLingua-2 vs perplexity-ranked LongCodeZip vs reranker-based SWE-Pruner) at roughly similar target ratios, but actual achieved token budgets differ substantially across methods, so ratio and method quality are confounded.
stop_detail: Offline: Oracle-guided Code Distillation decomposes each file into a tree of file/function/block units and searches (genetic algorithm then hierarchical delta-debugging to 1-minimality) for a minimal sufficient context validated by an LLM-patch-plus-test oracle; online: SWEzze, a LoRA-tuned Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B, scores segments and performs budget-aware greedy selection at inference (Sec. on OCD/SWEzze).
threats_to_datum: Extracted via automated WebFetch summarization of HTML rather than direct table inspection; baseline compression ratios are not budget-matched, so resolution-rate deltas confound compression aggressiveness with underlying method quality.

demote_reason: Full text confirms the middleware only performs cross-lingual translation and structural rewriting of the user's natural-language instruction text pre-flight (Sec. 3.1/3.3); the authors explicitly list 'repository-aware grounding of [CONTEXT] from static analysis' as future work, not part of this paper's contribution, so there is no repository code-context representation, retrieval, or structural token-budget mechanism addressed.

key_numbers.value: raw source 27/45 (60.0%) vs frontier NL summary 4/45 (8.9%) vs 3B-model summary 4/45 (8.9%) vs signature+docstring 6/45 (13.3%)

key_numbers.metric: resolve rate, N=70 oracle-localized multi-file subset
key_numbers.value: oracle_full 19/70 (27.1%) vs oracle_tier 23/70 (32.9%) vs oracle_keep_drop 25/70 (35.7%)
oracle_full ~25,426 vs oracle_tier ~8,629 vs oracle_keep_drop ~6,876

budget_tradeoff_detail: Skeleton and keep/drop representations resolve issues at roughly 27-38% fewer tokens than full source (6,876-8,629 vs 25,426 mean tokens) while matching or exceeding full-source resolve rate (32.9-35.7% vs 27.1%); NL summaries at ~180 tokens answer only 4/45 behavioral probes versus 27/45 for raw source at ~1,124 tokens (Table 2-3).
confound_note: Localization is held fixed via an oracle (gold-changed files identical across all arms), isolating representation as the manipulated variable; however token budget is NOT matched across arms — it varies naturally with each representation tier's information density (full-body > skeleton > signature > summary).
stop_detail: Sec. 3: deterministic AST extraction builds a Subsystem->Component->File->Class->Function tree; representation 'rungs' (full-body, method-only, UML-class-skeleton, signature+doc, name, exclude) deterministically reduce non-edited code while gold-edited units are kept verbatim ('keep/drop'); no LLM is used to build representations.
threats_to_datum: Numbers extracted via automated HTML-to-text summarization of a dense, notation-heavy preprint; the behavioral probe study (n=45, three held-out repos: seaborn/pylint/pytest) is small and may not generalize.

benchmarks: CodeNib Base (derived from SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Multilingual, 100 snapshots)

key_numbers.value: graph updates 8.7x faster, vector updates 25.4x faster than rebuild at median
4.7x median per-request latency ratio on 63% of 1,000 matched requests
50-87% fewer tokens than grep/read baseline within a 5% localization-quality margin (AnswerRecall@5), across 5 agent models

budget_tradeoff_detail: Eager/Compact context policies (frozen top-10 dense-retrieved code blocks) cut trajectory tokens 50-87% versus a grep/read baseline while staying within a 5% localization-quality margin (AnswerRecall@5), across five agent models (Sec. 7.4).
confound_note: Eager vs Compact holds retrieved candidates identical (same top-10 dense ranking) and isolates the context-retention/delivery policy (frozen injection vs one-time deterministic history rewrite) as a true budget-matched ablation; the further comparison against grep/read varies both retrieval mechanism and token budget together, conflating retrieval quality with delivery policy.
stop_detail: Sec. 7.4: 'Compact' applies a one-time deterministic history rewrite at first successful read, H_j -> H-hat_j = [s, q || d_j], replacing frozen top-10 dense-retrieved L2 code blocks plus discarded exploration turns with a deduplicated-path-plus-latest-result seed, enabling KV-cache reuse without LLM summarization.
threats_to_datum: Numbers extracted via automated HTML summarization of a long, notation-heavy preprint; per-model resolve/accuracy numbers were not reported (only trajectory-token counts), limiting judgment of whether token savings preserve downstream task success beyond the localization proxy metric.
